Maya — thanks, received the profile. I pulled the sample and ran a quick tokenization pass against the demo prompts you sent. High-level draft findings below; attaching a short spreadsheet (clearhealth_map_v1.xlsx) and more detailed cost notes (redwood_cost_assumptions.pdf).

Quick numbers (rough):
- Observed tokens/request (sample avg): 420 tokens/request (includes 280 tokens input avg + 140 tokens generations avg). Sample p95 = 1,120 tokens/request.
- Tokens per $ (hosted API, default model variant): ~12,800 tokens per $ at baseline (shared hosted pool pricing). This assumes no caching and 1:1 generation per request.

Scenarios with caching/batching:
- Prefix caching (route-level): expected to save ~18-25% of generation tokens for common queries in your profile (help text, repeated prompts).
- Per-customer KV-cache for session continuity: saves ~10-35% of tokens depending on session length; bigger wins on longer chat sessions.
- Prefetching + warm KV: reduces cold-start tokens for common continuations by ~30% on targeted flows.
- Batching (server-side continuous batching): at 10 RPS with conservative batch windows, we can reduce per-token runtime cost by ~12% (kernel-level throughput gains) with minimal added latency (avg +8–12ms).

Tradeoffs and latency:
- With batching enabled aggressively (batch window 25ms), you can see 50–80ms added median latency during low concurrency; at 10 RPS we recommend a smaller window (10–15ms), which yields ~6–10% cost savings and <30ms added tail.
- For your interactive SSO flow, to keep p95 < 300ms, we recommend: prefix cache enabled, conservative batching window (<=15ms), and enabling KV-cache for continuing sessions.

Dedicated vs Hosted one-liner for procurement:
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable tokens/$ (typically 20–35% lower unit compute cost depending on commit), and eliminates noisy-neighbor variability — cost benefit only realized at steady throughput and with commit term. Hosted: lowest friction and better for bursty early pilots but higher per-token unit.

Deliverables I will attach: short table with tokens/$ under three toggle states (no-cache/no-batch, cache only, cache+batches) and an ops note for latency tradeoffs. Will aim to get that by 5/20.

—Rishi

Team — finalizing the short table and answers; attaching the PDF with assumptions (redwood_cost_assumptions.pdf). Summary answers inline for procurement:

- Break-even math (30% prefix hit + 10% KV): effective tokens/request moves from 420 -> ~266 tokens/request. Under Hosted list assumptions that moves tokens/$ from ~12,800 -> ~20,000 tokens/$ (i.e., ~+56% tokens per $). If you switch to Dedicated with a 30% lower compute unit price, the Dedicated tokens/$ would be ~26,000 tokens/$ given the same cache hit-rate. So net delta: Dedicated gives ~+30% tokens/$ vs Hosted after caching.

- Evaluation vs production billing: we recommend treating eval windows as instrumented test runs and flagging them in the request headers (x-redwood-eval=true). For billing we will provide an eval adjustment that reports raw token counts separately and allows a one-time credit/discount if the eval spike exceeds agreed bounds. This keeps your production KPI comparables clean.

- Explicit matrix (attached): tokens/request (avg/p95) across cache hit-rate buckets (0/10/30/50%), and latency impact table for batch windows (10/15/25ms) across 1/10/50 RPS. Key recommendation: pilot mode = prefix cache ON, KV-cache ON, batching window = 12ms.

- 5/24: Redwood sends signed MAP addendum with the cache/batch ops notes (Rishi)
- 5/28: Procurement and Redwood finalize Dedicated vs Hosted commitment decision (ClearHealth)
- 6/01: Pilot starts (instrumentation with eval flag)

Attachments: redwood_cost_assumptions.pdf (assumptions & matrix), clearhealth_map_v1.xlsx (detailed numbers).
